amendments.because: A model's judgment can't be proven by required tests; a structural check is deterministic
amendments.done_when: The story template has a '## New and existing repos' section above Risks, saying what a fresh init or adoption gets, what an existing repo gets on upgrade, and naming a test for each; the cold read reports a story whose section is missing or covers only one side; the review instructions check the upgrade path of an existing repo; the fix brief and skill say a fix states both sides in one line. One command-level test: a cold read of a story without the section reports it.

amendments.because: The owner meant Forge's own features must consider new and existing client repos, not that every client story carries the section
amendments.done_when: The story template has a '## New and existing repos' section above Risks, saying what a fresh init or adoption gets, what an existing repo gets on upgrade, and naming a test for each; forge read refuses a story doc without that section with one plain line naming it, as it does for other malformed docs, and the cold-read instructions ask the reader to check both sides; the review instructions check the upgrade path of an existing repo; the fix brief and skill say a fix states both sides in one line. One command-level test: forge read on a story without the section refuses with that line.

done_when: This repo's AGENTS.md Review rules say a change to Forge states what new client repos (init or adoption) and existing client repos (on upgrade) each get and tests both, reporting a one-sided change as P1. Nothing changes for client repos' own stories.
why: Features get planned and reviewed for Forge's own repo or a fresh init only, so existing client repos on older Forge versions get skipped or broken on upgrade
